title.en: Practical 4: Exothermic or endothermic dissolution of a salt

text.en: Some salts make water warm when they dissolve and some make it cold.

The aim is to test whether the dissolution of a given salt is exothermic or endothermic. A process that releases heat is exothermic and one that absorbs heat is endothermic.
Take 50 ml of water in two beakers A and B and note the temperature. Add 5 g of sample A to beaker A, stir until it dissolves and note the final temperature; repeat with sample B.
If the temperature rises, the dissolution is exothermic; if it falls, it is endothermic. Sodium hydroxide and calcium oxide are examples that release heat, while ammonium nitrate absorbs heat.
